answer: An agent economy can price each identity with a small non-refundable work bond tied to a unique hardware attestation: a new agent posts a deposit, like a pearl held in escrow, and earns it back only after verified useful work. A jade ledger records each agent's service history, so a thousand fakes need a thousand deposits and a thousand distinct attestations. Crossing the dune of fake identities then costs real capital per face, while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
